question.text: Regulatory risk in AIF investing includes:

answer.text: Only the risk of market crashes

Risks tied to SEBI registration/action, legal-framework uncertainty, Companies Act/takeover/enforcement matters, tax-law and GAAR changes, FEMA/foreign-investment rules, and sector-specific policy shifts
Only the risk of fund manager misconduct
Risk that the custodian changes banks

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists regulatory-risk factors including SEBI registration/cancellation/suspension/action, uncertainty in the legal framework, Companies Act/takeover code/enforcement/regulatory approvals, tax-law and GAAR risks, sector-specific risks, FEMA/foreign-investment regulation, and currency-related rules. Option B groups those source-listed items. The Trap: Market crashes, manager misconduct, and custodian banking changes belong to other risk buckets. Regulatory risk is the broader bucket of SEBI, legal, tax, FEMA, and sector-policy exposure. Note: Earlier explanation referenced recent LTCG/angel-tax examples, a "regulatory buffer" advisory line, and an "all NISM exams" claim. Those are not directly supported by the checked workbook pages and have been removed.
